title: Field Report: jeton load_credentials mishandles token-less files — fix belongs in jeton repo (no .bon there)

brief.done: jeton loads and refreshes a token-less ADC-shaped file correctly and never writes a lossy shape back; test pinned in jeton's suite.
brief.how: In jeton: (1) refresh condition becomes `if not creds.valid and creds.refresh_token` (covers never-had-token as well as expired); (2) _save_credentials round-trips unknown fields from the source file (read-merge-write) or gains a persist=False param callers can set for caller-owned files. Add a unit test with an ADC-shaped fixture (no token, no expiry). jeton repo has no .bon — this item lives here as jeton's main consumer; do the work in ~/repos/spm1001/jeton.
brief.what: 1. Fix refresh condition in jeton auth.py. 2. Make save shape lossless or optional. 3. ADC-fixture unit test. 4. Bump mise's jeton dep if pinned; consider then retiring mise's guest-mode bypass or keeping it as defense-in-depth.
brief.why:
Found live 2026-06-10 under Cornichon guest mode. jeton/src/jeton/auth.py::load_credentials only refreshes when creds.expired — but google-auth reports expired=False when the file has NO expiry field, so an ADC-shaped authorized_user file (no token, no expiry) is returned as invalid -> None, misdiagnosed by callers as a revoked refresh token. Verified empirically: Credentials(token=None,...) gives expired=False, valid=False. Second hazard in the same path: the post-refresh _save_credentials writes jeton's token.json shape, silently dropping fields like type / quota_project_id / universe_domain — handed an ADC file, a successful refresh would corrupt it for any ADC consumer (e.g. an SDK reading GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS). Mise BYPASSES both in guest mode (adapters/http_client.py), but jeton itself remains wrong for any other consumer.
